question: Does the sole zero-row-selected weak-mend-persistence knob preserve the complete frozen current-main path at null and alter only existing Weak on living enemies after a successful in-combat heal when enabled?

scientificBasis.selection: The complete preregistered competing-options audit selected weak-mend-persistence as its only eligible structural option: 17 active, 23 exact-inactive and eight viable policies, all nine weak-source and recovery-card pairs, and separate two-sided Scoreline and Afterimage support.
scientificBasis.closedAlternatives: Voluntary-loss-recovery failed at six active and three viable policies. Recovery-repeated-hit failed at 15 active policies. Their frozen failures may not be subsetted, reordered, retuned or reopened.
scientificBasis.minimality: Reuse Emberheart ownership, the shared successful-heal law, existing Weak state, living-enemy filtering and existing STATUS events. Add one dormant-by-default integer field lookup in CombatRules.heal_player. Add no state, event type, policy hook, optimiser, payoff, card, relic or product text.
scientificBasis.claimBoundary: This is exact-null and direct-mediator identity evidence only. It cannot establish natural activation, acquisition, policy selection, complementarity, balance value, detector performance, product feasibility or acceptance.

candidate.primitive: After each successful in-combat player heal, add exactly one Weak to every living enemy that already has positive Weak.
candidate.implementationSite: CombatRules.heal_player after the existing positive-heal event and before its return.
candidate.observation: Focused controls read existing enemy status dictionaries and the existing HEAL and STATUS event queue directly. Whole-run identity reuses the previously identity-proved TURN, DRAW, PLAY, KINDLE, node, reward and boss-relic trace without adding telemetry.
excluded: post-combat healing where CombatState is null

emberHeartWeakMend.enabled: Integer one adds one Weak, through the existing status law, to each living enemy whose Weak is already positive after and only after actual in-combat healing is positive and Emberheart is owned.
emberHeartWeakMend.intendedMediator: Duration of already-present enemy Weak after successful in-combat healing.
emberHeartWeakMend.forbiddenDirectEffects: No HP amount, heal eligibility, enemy HP, non-Weak status, dead enemy, non-Weak enemy, post-combat heal, action path, card choice, reward choice, policy, RNG, Scoreline, Afterimage, acquisition or result may change directly.
emberHeartWeakMend.trustBoundary: Deterministic content construction accepts only integer 0 or 1; -1 and 2 must fail before Godot execution.

scorelinePayoff.fixed: Separate causal factor. No Scoreline payoff, Faultline scalar or related carrier varies in this preflight.

afterimagePayoff.fixed: Separate causal factor. No Afterimage payoff, Warden's Edge scalar or related carrier varies in this preflight.

acquisitionPriority.fixed: The exact frozen reward policy is unchanged.

wardSetupPriority.fixed: The exact frozen combat policy is unchanged.

designMeaning: This is a one-factor identity preflight, not the old four-factor design and not a causal factorial. Omitted and zero are intentional null aliases. Enabled occurs only on four fixed direct-mediator surfaces and never in a whole-run cell.

anchors.wholeRun: The exact identity-proved 64-policy by four-seed Duskblade Vow-5 co-hand trace. It freezes ordered nodes, turns, draws, plays, kindles, card rewards, boss relics, final RNG, resolved policy, package events and results.
anchors.eligibleControl: Emberheart owned; player at 10 of 20 HP; heal three; living Weak-2 and Weak-1 enemies, one living non-Weak enemy and one dead Weak-4 enemy.
anchors.noRelicControl: Ashwarden without Emberheart on the same state; enabled content must be exact-null.
anchors.noEffectiveHealControl: Emberheart owned at full HP on the same enemy state; actual heal zero must be exact-null.
anchors.postCombatControl: Emberheart owned; CombatState is null; run HP heals by three while the constructed combat state and queue remain exact-null.

estimands.nullEncodingIdentity: Exact canonical equality between omitted and explicit-zero rows for all 256 identities and all four focused surfaces.
estimands.rngIdentity: Exact final RNG cursor equality across anchor, omitted and explicit-zero for all identities.

estimands.negativeControls: Enabled is exact-null without Emberheart, without positive actual healing and when CombatState is null.
estimands.notEstimated: No whole-run enabled effect, natural activation count, payoff, acquisition effect, causal interaction, complementarity, policy repertoire, balance endpoint, detector endpoint or product endpoint.

mechanisticallyJustifiedInteractions: emberHeartWeakMend x recovery-card acquisition is mechanistically possible because an in-combat heal must occur; acquisition is fixed here.
emberHeartWeakMend x Weak setup is mechanistically possible because positive enemy Weak must pre-exist; setup policy is fixed here.

Scoreline payoff and Afterimage payoff remain distinct possible interference packages. Neither is varied, pooled or estimated here; any later shared anchor must measure decision value before a joint cell is allowed.

executionAndStopping.construction: Deterministic Python owns content construction, invalid-level rejection, complete plan construction, process execution, content-addressed caching, exact comparison and the stop/go decision.
executionAndStopping.order: Reject invalid levels first. Execute all 12 cheap focused controls. Only if every control passes, execute the complete 256-row omitted-null arm and complete 256-row explicit-zero arm. Compare both to the same frozen anchor.
executionAndStopping.firstLook: The fixed controls and two complete null arms are the only look. Stop at the first failed stage. There is no repair, rerun, reserve, row replacement, adaptive continuation or enabled whole-run cell.
executionAndStopping.stagedConstraint: The cheap direct-mediator stage may advance only to whole-run null identity. Whole-run null identity may advance only to a separately preregistered causal first look. No endpoint is claimed from an arm that was not comparably evaluated.
